nodes.title: Conductance, Conductivity & Cell Constant
points: Electrical Resistance: R = ρ (l / A). SI Unit: Ohm (Ω).
Conductance (G): Reciprocal of resistance: G = 1 / R. Unit: Ω⁻¹ or Siemens (S).
Conductivity / Specific Conductance (κ): Conductance of 1 cm³ of solution: κ = (1/R) · (l/A) = G · k_cell. Unit: Ω⁻¹ cm⁻¹ or S cm⁻¹ (SI: S m⁻¹).
Cell Constant (k_cell): Ratio of distance between electrodes to cross-sectional area: k_cell = l / A = R · κ. Unit: cm⁻¹ or m⁻¹.
Wheatstone Bridge method is used to measure resistance R of an electrolytic solution using AC source (to prevent electrolysis).

nodes.title: Molar Conductivity (Λ) & Dilution Effects
points: Molar Conductivity (Λ): Conducting power of all ions produced by dissolving 1 mole of electrolyte in solution: Λ = (1000 · κ) / C, where κ is in S cm⁻¹, C in mol L⁻¹ (M). Unit: S cm² mol⁻¹.
Effect of Dilution on Conductivity (κ): Conductivity κ DECREASES on dilution for both strong and weak electrolytes because the number of current-carrying ions per unit volume decreases.
Effect of Dilution on Molar Conductivity (Λ): Molar conductivity Λ INCREASES on dilution because total volume containing 1 mole increases more than κ decreases.
Debye-Hückel-Onsager Equation (Strong Electrolytes): Λ = Λ₀ − A √C. Plot of Λ vs √C is a straight line with intercept Λ₀ (molar conductivity at infinite dilution) and slope −A.

nodes.title: Kohlrausch's Law of Independent Migration
points: Statement: At infinite dilution, each ion migrates independently of its co-ion and makes a definite contribution to the total molar conductivity of the electrolyte.
Equation: Λ₀ = x λ₊° + y λ₋° for electrolyte A_x B_y.
Applications of Kohlrausch's Law:
1. Calculation of Λ₀ for weak electrolytes: Λ₀(CH₃COOH) = Λ₀(CH₃COONa) + Λ₀(HCl) − Λ₀(NaCl).
2. Degree of Dissociation of weak electrolyte: α = Λ / Λ₀.
3. Dissociation Constant of weak acid: K_a = (α² C) / (1 − α) = [C (Λ/Λ₀)²] / [1 − (Λ/Λ₀)].

nodes.title: Galvanic Cells & The Daniell Cell
points: Galvanic / Voltaic Cell: Converts chemical energy of a spontaneous redox reaction into electrical energy.
Daniell Cell Setup: Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(aq, 1 M) || Cu²⁺(aq, 1 M) | Cu(s).
• Anode (Oxidation, Negative terminal): Zn(s) ⟶ Zn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻.
• Cathode (Reduction, Positive terminal): Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ ⟶ Cu(s).
• Net Cell Reaction: Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) ⟶ Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s).

Salt Bridge: U-tube filled with agar-agar gel containing inert electrolyte (KCl, KNO₃, NH₄NO₃). Functions: (1) Maintains electrical neutrality, (2) Prevents liquid junction potential, (3) Completes circuit.
Standard Cell Potential: E°_cell = E°_cathode − E°_anode = E°_right − E°_left = +0.34 V − (−0.76 V) = +1.10 V.

nodes.title: Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE) & Series
points: Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE): Primary reference electrode. Reversible hydrogen electrode.
Representation: Pt(s) | H₂(g, 1 bar) | H⁺(aq, 1 M).
Assigned Potential: E° = 0.000 V at all temperatures.
Can act as anode (H₂ ⟶ 2H⁺ + 2e⁻) or cathode (2H⁺ + 2e⁻ ⟶ H₂).
Electrochemical Series: Arrangement of electrode systems in increasing order of their standard reduction potentials (E°).
• Top: Strong reducing agents (Li⁺/Li = −3.05 V, readily oxidized).
• Bottom: Strong oxidizing agents (F₂/F⁻ = +2.87 V, readily reduced).
A metal with lower E° displaces a metal with higher E° from its salt solution.

formulas.label: Displacement rule
formulas.expr: Lower E° (active metal) displaces higher E° ion

nodes.title: Nernst Equation & Equilibrium Constant
points: Nernst Equation for Half-Cell (Mⁿ⁺ + n e⁻ ⟶ M): E = E° − (0.0592 / n) log₁₀(1 / [Mⁿ⁺]) at 298 K.
Nernst Equation for Complete Cell: E_cell = E°_cell − (0.0592 / n) log₁₀ Q, where Q is reaction quotient = [Products] / [Reactants].
At Equilibrium: E_cell = 0 and Q = K_eq.
Equilibrium Constant Formula: log₁₀ K_eq = (n · E°_cell) / 0.0592 at 298 K.
Gibbs Energy and Cell Potential: ΔG° = −n F E°_cell.
Spontaneity criterion: E°_cell > 0 ⟹ ΔG° < 0 (spontaneous reaction).

nodes.title: Electrolysis & Faraday's Laws
points: Electrolysis: Non-spontaneous redox reaction driven by external electrical energy in an electrolytic cell.
Faraday's First Law: Mass of substance deposited (W) is directly proportional to quantity of electricity (Q):
W = Z · Q = Z · I · t, where Z = Electrochemical Equivalent = (Molar mass) / (n · F).
Faraday's Constant: 1 F = charge of 1 mole electrons ≈ 96500 C mol⁻¹.
Faraday's Second Law: When same quantity of electricity is passed through different electrolytes in series: W₁ / E₁ = W₂ / E₂.
Electrolysis Products:
• Molten NaCl: Na at cathode, Cl₂ at anode.
• Aqueous NaCl: H₂ at cathode (higher reduction potential than Na⁺), Cl₂ at anode (overvoltage of O₂).

nodes.title: Commercial Batteries, Fuel Cells & Corrosion
points: Primary Batteries: Dry cell (Leclanché cell, 1.5 V), Mercury cell (1.35 V, stable voltage, used in hearing aids). Non-rechargeable.
Secondary Batteries (Rechargeable): Lead Storage Battery (used in automobiles):
• Anode: Pb(s); Cathode: PbO₂(s); Electrolyte: 38% H₂SO₄ (density 1.28 g/cm³).
• Discharge reaction: Pb(s) + PbO₂(s) + 2H₂SO₄(aq) ⟶ 2PbSO₄(s) + 2H₂O(l) (E_cell ≈ 2.0 V per cell, 12 V for 6 cells). Charging reverses reaction.
H₂-O₂ Fuel Cell: Converts chemical energy of combustion directly into electricity: 2H₂ + O₂ ⟶ 2H₂O. High efficiency (~70%), eco-friendly (used in Apollo space program).

Corrosion of Iron (Rusting): Electrochemical process. Anode: Fe(s) ⟶ Fe²⁺ + 2e⁻; Cathode: O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ ⟶ 2H₂O. Rust formula: Fe₂O₃ · xH₂O. Prevention: Galvanization (Zn coating), sacrificial anode (Mg, Zn blocks).

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Derivations & Diagrams
points: Board Favourite #1: Derive Nernst equation for cell potential and obtain expression for equilibrium constant log₁₀ K_eq = (n E°_cell) / 0.0592.
Board Favourite #2: State and explain Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions. How is it used to determine Λ₀ of acetic acid?
Board Favourite #3: Draw neat labeled diagram of Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE) and write its electrode reactions.
Board Favourite #4: Describe the construction, working, and discharging/charging reactions of Lead Storage Battery.
Board Favourite #5: State and explain Faraday's first and second laws of electrolysis with mathematical expressions.

formulas.label: Nernst derivation
formulas.expr: ΔG = ΔG° + RT ln Q ⟹ −nFE = −nFE° + RT ln Q

formulas.label: K_eq derivation
formulas.expr: At equilibrium E = 0 ⟹ E° = (0.0592 / n) log K_eq

nodes.title: MHT-CET Shortcuts, Nernst Traps & Faraday Hacks
points: Intensive Property Trap: E°_cell is an INTENSIVE property! Never multiply E° when multiplying a half-reaction by a stoichiometric coefficient (e.g., if Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻ ⟶ Zn has E° = −0.76 V, then 2Zn²⁺ + 4e⁻ ⟶ 2Zn ALSO has E° = −0.76 V!).
ΔG° is EXTENSIVE: ΔG° = −n F E°_cell (depends on n).
Nernst Reaction Quotient Exponent Trap: For Al | Al³⁺ || Cu²⁺ | Cu: Reaction is 2Al + 3Cu²⁺ ⟶ 2Al³⁺ + 3Cu ⟹ Q = [Al³⁺]² / [Cu²⁺]³ and n = 6!
Faraday Mass Shortcut: Mass deposited W = (Molar mass × I × t) / (n × 96500).
Electricity to Deposit 1 Mole: 1 mole Ag⁺ = 1 F; 1 mole Cu²⁺ = 2 F; 1 mole Al³⁺ = 3 F.

formulas.label: E° intensive trap
formulas.expr: E° never multiplied by stoichiometric factor

formulas.label: Charge required
formulas.expr: Q(Coulombs) = n × 96500 C per mole of metal
